newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Overdue bills may scrub Venezuela FY97 surplus.
newsitem.headline: Overdue bills may scrub Venezuela FY97 surplus.

text.p: Past-due bills owed by the Venezuelan government could endanger its projected fiscal surplus for this year, a highly-placed Congressional source said.
"The government is talking about a fiscal surplus, but by having these fiscal credits pending what it's doing is juggling statistics," the source told reporters.
Among those bills is a 490 billion bolivar ($1 billion) tax refund owed to state oil company Petroleos de Venezuela (PdVSA), PdVSA president Luis Giusti said over the weekend.

The amount owed to PdVSA is equivalent to over one percent of gross domestic product (GDP). Venezuelan officials have said they expect to end the year with a budget surplus equivalent to 0.8 percent of GDP.

Venezuela is facing other bills that will hurt its finances, the source said. The Treasury owes money for goods and services totaling some 800 billion bolivars ($1.7 billion), Congressional sources said.

Last year, Venezuela won plaudits from international investors when its budget surplus reached 0.9 percent of GDP -- erasing 1995's 4.8 percent of GDP deficit -- largely on high international oil prices.

On the PdVSA tax refund, Giusti said he has asked the government to resolve the problems of the "draw backs," or refunds made available to all exporters. The draw backs are often paid late, and in bolivars devalued by inflation that topped 103 percent last year.
"We are in running discussions to solve once and for all the problems that all exporters have with the system," Giusti told reporters.
